findings.title: Dedent byte ranges must be expanded to grapheme boundaries before deletion and cursor mapping
findings.evidence: A leading ASCII space followed by U+0301 forms one grapheme. count=1 creates 0..1, but TextEditorCore::select_range floors both ends, collapsing selection to 0..0. Paste("") deletes nothing, while the implementation maps cursor offsets as if one byte was removed and increments generation. Independent real-Runtime test on candidate fails: source=" \u{301}value", actual unchanged, expected "value". Frozen TextBuffer::remove_range expands its end with ceil_boundary; the exact frozen primitive source and dedent loop pass all three combining-indentation cases. Two spaces followed by a combining mark also require using actual expanded range lengths for mapping.
findings.requested_fix: Construct actual grapheme-safe removal ranges matching frozen floor/ceil semantics before mapping original cursor/anchor. Apply edits through the existing core. Add real-Runtime regressions for one/two spaces with attached combining marks, multiline selections and unselected cursor lines, preserving selection direction, generation and cursor offsets.
